sentences.show: One of the most famous photos ever taken was a single shot, with no light meter.
Ansel Adams took it on this day in 1941.
The government had hired him to photograph its national lands.
Late in the afternoon in New Mexico, he saw it: a village, white crosses, and the moon rising.
He pulled off the road at Hernandez, and grabbed his camera.
Then the problem. He couldn't find his light meter.
The sun was slipping away. He was desperate.
Then he remembered how bright the moon was: 250 candles per square foot.
He worked out the exposure, and took one picture.
He tried a second shot. The light had left the crosses. A few seconds too late.
That lone negative became Moonrise. Adams printed it over 1,300 times.
Also on this day: Australia's first troops sailed to war, and the European Union was born.
